THE `format IS NULL OR format = ''` UPDATE IS DEAD CODE ON A CHAIN-BUILT TARGET AND IS KEPT FOR EXACTLY ONE REASON. `ADD COLUMN ... NOT NULL DEFAULT 'blog'` gives every existing row `'blog'` on PostgreSQL 11+, so the statement matches ZERO rows there. It is retained because DB-002 established that some versions on hosted targets were applied by raw Management API SQL, so a target can carry this column out of band and nullable; without the UPDATE such a target's NULL rows would make this file's own `VALIDATE CONSTRAINT` fail. Change-guarded and idempotent either way.

THE CONSTRAINT GUARD IS SCOPED TO `conrelid`, WHICH IS A CORRECTION TO THE ARCHIVED FILE. The archive's guard was a bare `WHERE conname = 'artist_blog_posts_format_check'` across every schema in the database, so an unrelated constraint with that name anywhere would have made the add skip silently. Scoped to `'public.artist_blog_posts'::regclass`, that cannot happen. The post-condition additionally requires `convalidated`, because a `NOT VALID` constraint that was never validated is the 'written down but not executing' shape this repository has now found three times and it would be invisible here.

`ADD CONSTRAINT ... NOT VALID` then `VALIDATE CONSTRAINT` is the lock shape, not a stylistic choice. NOT VALID takes ACCESS EXCLUSIVE briefly and skips the scan; VALIDATE takes the weaker SHARE UPDATE EXCLUSIVE and does the scan. Both are inside the migration's own transaction, so a target that cannot reach the asserted state fails the apply rather than reporting success. `scripts/ci/check-migration-validation.mjs` independently requires NOT VALID or a reviewed lock-budget marker for a CHECK added to an existing table, and this is the former.

execution.resumeStrategy: Authored - manual apply pending (CP-051). One transaction, one file. The five ADD COLUMNs take ACCESS EXCLUSIVE on public.artist_blog_posts; on PostgreSQL 11+ a NOT NULL column with a DEFAULT does not rewrite the table, so the lock is held for the catalog work only and is independent of table size. ADD CONSTRAINT ... NOT VALID holds ACCESS EXCLUSIVE without scanning. VALIDATE CONSTRAINT holds SHARE UPDATE EXCLUSIVE for one scan. CREATE INDEX (not CONCURRENTLY, because the file must be one transaction) holds SHARE on the table for the build. On a large `artist_blog_posts` the index build is the only step that scales with row count, and it is the one to watch in the statement timeout. Safe to apply BEFORE any consumer change and in any order relative to the other two DB-019 files: this file touches only `artist_blog_posts`, 20260927130100 only the two new news preference tables, and 20260927130200 only the `music_tracks` view.
execution.idempotency: Deterministic and repeatable, verified by applying the file THREE times consecutively on a throwaway PostgreSQL 16.15 cluster: every apply exited 0 and the surviving column set, constraint (convalidated=true), index and post-condition result were identical after each. ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS x5, a `pg_constraint` existence guard scoped to `conrelid`, VALIDATE CONSTRAINT on an already-validated constraint (a documented no-op), two change-guarded UPDATEs, CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS and COMMENT ON COLUMN are each individually re-runnable.

quarantine.strategy: No data movement, no batch, no quarantine table. The one data write is a single change-guarded UPDATE over rows this file has just created a column for, so there is no partial-application state: the file is one transaction and its own post-condition RAISEs if the asserted state is unreachable, so a half-applied column set cannot be committed. If the operator must stop mid-file for lock reasons, the transaction rolls back whole and the file is re-run from the top - there is no cursor to resume from because there is no committed prefix.
quarantine.lockBudget: The `format` / `status` / `published_at desc nulls last` index is the only access path the feed's query shape gains, and it is the only step whose duration scales with the table. The two UPDATEs scan the table but write only the rows the guard selects, and both are on the same column set the ALTER has already touched, so they hit warm pages. The CHECK validation is a single sequential scan with no writes. No statement here holds a lock while waiting on a second lock, so there is no deadlock ordering to get wrong.

constraints: ONE constraint is added: `artist_blog_posts_format_check CHECK (format IN ('blog','article','press_release')) NOT VALID`, immediately validated in the same transaction. The existing `artist_blog_posts_status_check` (20260702210503:21), `artist_blog_posts_posted_as_type_check` (:64-68), the primary key and the unique slug are untouched.

The guard is `IF NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM pg_constraint WHERE conname = 'artist_blog_posts_format_check' AND conrelid = 'public.artist_blog_posts'::regclass)`. Scoping to `conrelid` is a correction to the archived file, whose bare `conname` match would skip the add if an unrelated constraint anywhere in the database carried that name.

The post-condition requires `convalidated`, so a constraint that was added but never validated fails the apply rather than sitting there looking correct. This is the 'written down but not executing' class the repository has found three times (CP-104, `staff_performance_metrics`, `staff_shifts`): here it would be completely invisible, because the constraint name and its presence both look right.

The post-condition also requires the resolved type of `format` to be exactly `text` and of `distribution` to be exactly `jsonb`. A target that received either column out of band as a domain or a varchar would otherwise change what PostgREST can serialize, silently.
indexes: ONE index is added: `idx_artist_blog_posts_format_status_published on public.artist_blog_posts (format, status, published_at desc nulls last)`, byte-identical to the archived migration's. It serves the news feed's actual shape, `.eq('status','published').in('format',['article','blog']).order('published_at', asc:false)`, which without it falls back to a sort over every published row. Created non-CONCURRENTLY because the file must be one transaction; on a large table the operator should expect this statement to dominate the apply and should NOT wrap it in a CONCURRENTLY variant, because doing so would put CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY outside a transaction block.
NO index is added for `subtitle`, `boilerplate` or `embargo_until`. No consumer filters on them: `embargo_until` is read for display only, and the other two are read by id.
constraintsAndIndexes.validationPlan: The file's own post-condition DO block is the target-side validation and is proven able to FAIL in the two ways that matter, measured by executing the extracted block standalone against a deliberately broken state: (1) with `format` retyped to `varchar(10)`, it raised `public.artist_blog_posts.format is character varying(10) not text`; (2) with the CHECK dropped and one row carrying `format='weekly_digest'`, it raised `1 artist_blog_posts rows still carry a format outside PRESS_FORMATS`; and it returned GREEN on the healthy post-state and GREEN again after a re-apply restored each broken state. Stated honestly about reach: assertion (2) is unreachable while the CHECK is present AND validated, because PostgreSQL itself prevents that state - it defends an out-of-band target, it is not proof that the backfill ran. The backfill is proven by the measured distribution value before and after, and by the Layer 0 query. NO committed contract-test `.sql` file is provided for this migration: `supabase/tests/` is outside DB-019's working set, and a contract test that this task cannot also place under `supabase/tests/` would be a second mechanism the discover lane's guard would have to learn about. Two shapes are already anticipated by this file's own post-condition, so a bad forward fix cannot be applied silently: a CHECK left unvalidated, or a column left at the wrong type, both RAISE. A correct re-application of THIS file also restores any state its post-condition rejects, which is verified - each negative control above was followed by a re-apply that returned the post-condition to GREEN.

TWO DEFECTS IN THIS LANE'S OWN WORK WERE FOUND BY RUNNING THE FILE, and both are recorded because the shape is reusable. (1) The header comment block had a line that lost its `--` prefix, so the migration failed to parse at byte 91 with a syntax error on the word `gates`. A header comment is not a comment if one line in it is not prefixed, and no static gate in this repository checks that. (2) A first draft of the post-condition's row assertion was placed AFTER the constraint assertion, so the control that exercised it fired on the constraint message instead and the row assertion was never measured. The order is now data-first, and the controls are re-run and green.
